newsitem.title: USA: Rich US corp bond deals makes buyers more choosy.
newsitem.headline: Rich US corp bond deals makes buyers more choosy.

text.p: Aggressive pricing by dealers coupled with the massive amount of new supply has made buyers of U.S. corporate bonds more choosy and added a greater element of uncertainty for new issues, syndicate sources said.

"There has definitely been a change for the worse in market sentiment," said one high-yield bond syndicate official. "There is still several billion dollars of new supply coming by the Fourth of July and the market now feels a little bit soft."
She said the dip in Treasury and stock prices also eroded the positive investor sentiment seen at the start of the week.
The closely-watched junk bond mutual fund cash flows by AMG Data Services provided little solace this week.
AMG reported net cash inflows into junk bond funds slowed to $128.3 million in the latest week, compared to $457.7 million and $627.4 million in prior two weeks.

"This lower number suggests that cash flows are slowly starting to abate," said one trader "People aren't going to invest in high-yield if (prices in) our market do nothing but go up, like the stock market."
Meanwhile, low yields offered on many new high-yield bond issues began to discourage wary portfolio managers.
Several recently priced issues such as Ocean Energy Inc's $200 million in B3/B-minus rated 10-year senior subordinated notes traded down in the secondary market.
One portfolio manager noted new issues from single-B-rated energy companies like Ocean Energy Inc have priced at levels more typical of double-B credits.
Despite the cooler conditions in the new issue market, several junk bond deals are expected to price on Friday:
-Boyd Gaming Corp 's $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes (B1/BB-minus) via Salomon Brothers Inc.
Price talk on the deal is 312.5 basis points to 337.5 basis points over Treasuries.
-Glasstech Inc plans to sell $70 million in 10-year senior notes (B2/B-plus) via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities.
-West Coast Entertainment Corp is expected to sell $110 million in seven-year senior notes (B2/B) via Credit Suisse First Boston. Price talk on the deal is 10.625 percent ot 10.875 percent.
This morning, Archibald Candy Corp sold $100 million in seven-year senior secured notes (B2/B) via Jefferies & Co Inc. The deal is priced to yield 10.25 percent.
The offering was increased from an original size of $85 million but was priced on the wide end of price talk.
A trader at Jefferies said the deal, which priced at par, was bid at 101 soon after pricing.
